message.content: I've reviewed the artifact context already loaded. The key observation: the kernel computes the destination slot from per-view anchor magnitudes, so the applied permutation (and sign) is view-dependent, while the contract demands one shared signed permutation across both views. The initial probe only checked per-view best-fits (which passed with different transforms per view) plus a Gram error that is invariant to permutations — so it cannot detect the shared-transform violation. Zero columns likely mask most of the mismatch. I'll record this in the description model.

message.reasoning_content: Analyze: kernel does per-view column permutation based on anchor magnitude rank — view-dependent permutation! Contract requires ONE shared transform across both views. Probe found different transforms per view (permutation [1,0,2,3] vs [0,2,1,3]) — evidence the transform is view-dependent. Also zero columns: features[0,:,2:]=0, features[1,:,(0,3)]=0. In view 1, columns 0 and 3 are zero; anchors from same RNG stream (independent normals). The slot ranking uses anchors, and slot determined by rank of |anchor|. Note: since anchors differ per view, the slot map differs per view → view-dependent transform. Whether a single shared transform exists depends on which columns are zero. View 0 has columns 2,3 zero; view 1 has columns 0,3 zero. Column 3 zero in both. Kernel maps column c (per view) to slot = rank of |anchor_v,c|. Because permutation differs per view, generically no shared transform exists; but zero columns might mask it. Columns nonzero in both views: 1 and 2? View 0 nonzero: 0,1; view 1 nonzero: 1,2. Overlap: column 1 only (column 3 zero both). So most mismatch masked except column 1's placement and signs. Actually sign applies to values*sign — the shared transform sign for the only shared nonzero column 1 may differ between views. So the probe's per-view pass may hide a joint-failure. Record description.
